_note: pip install crafter. This is the paradigm's level 4 (survival), which is stock crafter: hostiles on, health/food/drink/energy decay, death ends the episode, nothing hidden from the HUD. Levels 1-3 freeze or remove parts of that and belong in a gymnasium.Wrapper shipped with the env, not here: an adapter that added them would stop humans and models from playing the same game.
_keys_note: Crafter's Discrete(17) map is 0=noop, 1=move_left, 2=move_right, 3=move_up, 4=move_down, 5=do, 6=sleep, 7=place_stone, 8=place_table, 9=place_furnace, 10=place_plant, 11=make_wood_pickaxe, 12=make_stone_pickaxe, 13=make_iron_pickaxe, 14=make_wood_sword, 15=make_stone_sword, 16=make_iron_sword. Curriculum 'keys' are Discrete action indices and here they restate the adapter default, so all 17 actions are reachable; noop is 'no key held'. On a button box with fewer buttons, cut 'keys' down and cut the Controls text with it, by hand.
_pacing_note: fps is the env step rate, so it sets how fast the survival clock runs against scanner time. 5 is what crafter's own interactive player uses (run_gui.py, --fps default 5), which is the only human-play cadence the engine actually documents; slowing to 2.5 buys 400 ms a decision at the cost of halving the game clock, so treat it as a knob rather than a constant. turn_based is false on purpose: with hostiles and homeostatic decay, freezing the world until the subject presses a key would remove the survival pressure and decouple game time from scanner time. latched_keys makes each frame prefer a fresh keydown over the held-key poll, so a tap shorter than one frame is not dropped, which is what run_gui.py does. One action per frame, last press wins.
_state_note: state_stride 50 = one pickled savestate (~145 KB) every 10 s at 5 fps, counted per episode; a measured 300 s block held 36 anchors, 5.2 MB raw and 0.7 MB inside the compressed npz. Each is an exact branch point for analysis or a model rollout. log_frames stores the displayed pixels too, zlib'd per frame (6.5 KB median in daylight, ~5 ms of the 200 ms frame; crafter mixes per-pixel noise into the view at night, so night frames reach 210 KB, and the measured block came to 1506 frames / 30 MB of pixels in a 27 MB npz). They are stored because stock crafter does NOT replay exactly: it rebalances creatures every tenth step by iterating a Python set of objects, so the despawn choice follows object id() and two runs of the same seed and actions diverge from step 10 on (terrain is identical; creatures are not). Sorting that list by position fixes it, which is a one-line change to crafter itself and belongs in a fork shared with the model harness. Until that lands, the stored frames rather than a replay are the record of what the subject saw.
